Subject: Initial perf targets & staging access for onboarding runs

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team here at Nimbus is excited to get the integration into our staging environment. Before we kick off the implementation, we want to align on pass/fail criteria for the onboarding performance work. High level:

- Target baseline: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for generation requests of ~256 tokens at steady state.
- Throughput goal: sustain 400 rps (requests per second) for 30 minutes during the acceptance window with error rate < 1%.
- Burst: tolerate 800 rps for up to 2 minutes with graceful degradation (queueing/fallback)

We can provide a staging dataset and an API key scoped to staging. Attached is a short spreadsheet with representative prompts and expected average output lengths. Can your team share a proposed load plan and a convenient 2-hour window next week?

Also please confirm what artifacts you’ll deliver after the run (raw logs, percentile breakdowns, KV/cache hit rates, and a brief summary).

Appreciate it — Sarah

--

Hi Sarah — great to get the targets. We're aligned on the acceptance artifacts you listed. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Pre-check (30m): validate staging environment (network, token throughput, model variant parity).
2) Baseline run (30m): ramp to 200 rps to capture steady-state latency and cache warmup.
3) Sustained run (30m): ramp to target 400 rps, hold for 30 minutes, collect percentiles and KV cache metrics.
4) Burst simulation (10 mins): short bursts to 800 rps to validate graceful degradation configuration.
5) Post-run: quick analysis + share artifacts (raw request/response csv, p50/p90/p95/p99, failure logs, routing decisions).

Deliverables: 1-page run summary, raw csv, and our recommended tuning changes (batching/quantization/routing). I'm attaching the detailed load plan and the mutual action plan for the onboarding (mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

Proposed windows: Thu 2026-11-26 09:00–11:00 PST or Mon 2026-11-30 13:00–15:00 PST. Which works for you?

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Run results: Thu baseline + Mon sustain summary and next steps

Hi Sarah/Javier — thanks for the run windows and staging access. Quick summary of what we ran and the initial results (full artifacts attached):

Runs executed:
- Thu 2026-11-26 09:10–10:05 PST: baseline + short burst validation (ramp to 200rps, two 1-min bursts at 800rps).
- Mon 2026-11-30 13:10–14:40 PST: sustained run to 400rps held for ~30 minutes.

Key findings:
- Sustained target: 400 rps held successfully for 30 minutes. p95 latency = 270ms, p99 = 520ms, error rate = 0.7%.
- Baseline: cold-starts pushed p95 to ~420ms during first 4 minutes; after warmup p95 fell below 300ms.
- Burst behavior: short 800rps bursts led to queueing and degraded p99 to ~1.2s, but error rate stayed <2% because we triggered the secondary routing policy (fallback model variant with lower throughput cost).
- KV cache hit ratio averaged 62% during sustained period; increasing prefix caching would likely drop p95 by ~30ms for this workload.

Artifacts delivered: stress-run-raw.csv (per-request logs), pctl_breakdown.pdf, and an initial tuning notes doc. See attachments.

Recommended follow-ups (next 2 weeks):
1) Autoscaler tweak: conservative reduced cold-starts by pre-warming on our dedicated pool — Marcus to propose exact settings.
2) Prefix cache policy: increase cache TTL for common prompts — Dev to run a short A/B test.
3) SLA gating: adjust canary routing so that burst fallbacks route to the cheaper variant only after p95 > 350ms for 60s (Lauren to own rollout).

If these look reasonable we can capture them in the mutual-action-plan and close the onboarding acceptance criteria. Would you like a short 30-minute readout this week?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: stress-run-raw.csv; pctl_breakdown.pdf; tuning_notes.md
